headline: Printmaking lets artists multiply their work—creating many originals from a single design
universal_truth: Reproduction changes access; what was rare for one becomes available to many
fun_facts: Before printmaking, every book had to be copied by hand—one at a time
Woodblock printing in China predates European printing by about 400 years
Andy Warhol's screen prints made 'multiple originals' a central artistic statement
discussion_questions: Is a print as 'original' as a painting?
How did the ability to reproduce images change culture?
What else in life becomes more valuable when shared?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Before printing, every image had to be made one at a time—paintings were unique, books were hand-copied. Printmaking changed everything: create once, reproduce many. A single design could become hundreds of identical images.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Printing seems mechanical—press ink onto paper. But printmaking is a creative art form with its own techniques and aesthetics. What makes printmaking different from other visual arts?
cliff.prompt: What makes printmaking unique as an art form?

options.text: The artist creates in reverse—carving or drawing on a surface to make an image that transfers to paper as a mirror image
options.response: Yes. Printmakers think backwards—cutting away what stays white, inking what prints. This reversed thinking produces distinctive results.

options.text: Printmaking is faster than painting or drawing
options.response: Speed helps with reproduction, but the real distinction is the reversed creative process...

q1.title: Thinking Backwards
q1.script: Printmakers work in reverse. Letters must be carved backwards. What's cut away stays white; what remains takes ink. This mirror-image thinking is challenging but creates effects impossible in direct drawing.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Thinking Backwards"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Multiple Originals
q2.script: Each print from a plate is an original—not a copy. Artists sign and number prints: 5/50 means the fifth print of fifty. Limited editions preserve value while allowing wider distribution. Originality multiplied.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Democratic Art
q3.script: Prints democratized art. When paintings belonged only to the wealthy, prints brought images to ordinary people. Books, posters, newspapers—printmaking made visual culture accessible to everyone.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Reproduction changes access. Printmaking shows that what was rare for one becomes available to many. Sharing multiplies rather than divides. Some things gain value through wider distribution.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 155. Tomorrow, we'll explore thinking with lines—drawing. Until then, consider what you create that could be shared with many.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Shareable Creation - Multiply Your Impact
growTrack.learning_objective: Consider how to share your work more widely
growTrack.activity: What do you create that could be reproduced? Ideas, designs, systems, content? Like printmakers, consider how creating once and sharing many could multiply your impact. What could you 'print'?
